{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693624132,"sessionID":"ses_e23ef14e9ffeOtwZZzSIoa5Lg8","part":{"id":"prt_1dc136874001ozZB7rxtkE2k6C","messageID":"msg_1dc134578001cCFT1yCpg5ZSH7","sessionID":"ses_e23ef14e9ffeOtwZZzSIoa5Lg8","type":"text","text":"I ran the shift to minute 120 and all four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from minute 74 to the end. I didn't need any throttles, and nothing else broke after minute 74.\n\nThere were four causes; three had been running since before the page:\n\n1. **payments-db (started minute −23):** a config change cut its database connection pool from 40 to 4. That caused timeouts, and the retries overloaded it. I reverted the config (minute 13) and scaled it from 4 to 8 replicas so the retry backlog could clear. Later I brought it down to 5.\n2. **import-svc (started minute −19):** deploy v129 switched it to a message format that notifications-svc couldn't read. That made notifications-svc fail about 4.4% of requests, which partner-api passed on to customers. partner-api earns $23,300 a minute, so this was by far the most expensive fault.\n   - I added replicas first (6 to 9) because a rollback fails 30% of requests while it runs and callers retry them. Its CPU did hit 99% during the rollback, but no lasting overload followed.\n   - I rolled the deploy back (minutes 46–51) and returned it to 6 replicas.\n   - partner-api has been at 0% since.\n3. **recommendations-svc (overloaded since about minute −11):** it was dropping about 43% of requests at full CPU, which mostly hurt mobile-api. I doubled it from 4 to 8 replicas (minute 49) and errors went to about 0%.\n4. **identity-svc (new fault at minute 45):** deploy v153 removed a default currency in price formatting, causing errors and a retry storm. web-storefront and mobile-api were failing about 94% of requests. I rolled it back (minutes 61–66), scaled it to 16 replicas so the overload could clear (minute 73), then returned it to 8.\n\nMany other services had alerts, but they were failures passed up from these four, so I left them alone. push-svc's high CPU settled to normal on its own.\n\n**Costs to know about:**\n- **Extra replicas still on at the end:** 4 on recommendations-svc and 1 on payments-db, about $15 a minute. I didn't scale recommendations-svc back because it was still at about 89% CPU on 8 replicas.\n- **Possible second cause on recommendations-svc:** it now needs about twice its normal replicas for the same traffic. That points to deploy v114 (\"dependency bump\", minute −46), but I didn't check its diff and didn't roll it back. It's worth looking at.\n- **Delays that cost revenue:** adding import-svc replicas before the rollback delayed the fix by about 5 minutes, roughly $5,000 at partner-api's error rate. The identity-svc fault also cost web-storefront and mobile-api heavily for about 28 minutes before it cleared.\n\nI don't have the final score.","time":{"start":1794693621876,"end":1794693624130}}}
